blocks.x: Fraud & Financial Crime Decisioning exists because a specific failure keeps repeating: fraud moves at event speed while defenses run batch; false positives burn good customers; investigations drown; regulators want the decision trail.
Fraud moves at event speed while defenses run batch; false positives burn good customers; investigations drown; regulators want the decision trail.

The pattern behind Fraud & Financial Crime Decisioning: decisions that should be systematized are still assembled by hand — one document, one queue, one meeting at a time. This solution replaces the assembly with a governed composition.

We build the streaming decision hub: features at event time, models + policy layers with champion-challenger, network analytics for organized fraud, and decision replay that answers auditors in minutes.
For Fraud & Financial Crime Decisioning, the components, as they land:

items: sub-second scoring with policy and replay
model and policy improvement on evidence
watchlist and monitoring within the hub

blocks.x: Fraud & Financial Crime Decisioning composes Dataq Nexus, Dataq Forge — platforms with documented controls and evidence packs, so governance is part of the runtime. The pattern is in delivery now in Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Logistics & Supply Chain, Technology & SaaS.

The Fraud & Financial Crime Decisioning engagement opens with the problem stated in the CFO's units and a baseline signed by whoever owns the number. Design follows with the risk envelope explicit; the proof phase runs a bounded slice on your data with falsifiable gate criteria; industrialization scales only what the evidence supports. In Fraud & Financial Crime Decisioning programs the same rule applies: every artifact ships with its evidence — who signed the baseline, what the gate measured, where the number lives.
